name: Chicken Foot
description: Chicken Foot is a domino game that originated in Texas or Mexico. It is a variation of Maltese Cross played with a double-9 or larger domino set. The game gets its name from the shape formed when a double is played - the next three tiles must be played on the double, creating a chicken foot shape.

content.text: Chicken Foot is a domino game that originated in Texas or Mexico. It is a variation of Maltese Cross played with a double-9 or larger domino set. The game gets its name from the shape formed when a double is played - the next three tiles must be played on the double, creating a chicken foot shape.

Country/Region of Origin: Texas/Mexico
Time Period: Late 20th century
Historical Development: Developed as a variation of Maltese Cross dominoes. The distinctive 'chicken foot' shape created by playing on doubles gives the game its name.
Cultural Significance: Popular domino game in the southern United States and Mexico. Often played socially in homes and community gatherings.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 8
Optimal Players: 4-6
Partnerships: Optional in some variants

Type: Double-9 domino set (55 tiles)
Alternative: Double-12 (91 tiles) for more players
Tiles: Each player draws specific number based on player count

Double-9 or double-12 domino set
Score sheet
Table space for layout

Tiles per Player varies by number of players:
2 players: 12-15 tiles each
3 players: 10-11 tiles each
4 players: 9-10 tiles each
5-6 players: 7-8 tiles each
7-8 players: 6-7 tiles each
Remaining tiles form the 'chicken yard' (boneyard)
